h_regions.name: Established human disease gene
h_regions.description: Human patient reports with pathogenic PSMF1 variants and phenotypic expansion that establish AMC8 as a Mendelian disorder.

h_regions.name: Perinatal neuromuscular spectrum
h_regions.description: Reports emphasizing perinatal lethality, fetal akinesia, congenital contractures, or arthrogryposis within the PSMF1 disorder spectrum.

h_regions.name: Functional disease mechanism
h_regions.description: Studies of disease-causing PSMF1 variants in patient cells or model organisms that explain how the variants disrupt proteostasis, mitochondria, or neurodevelopment.

h_regions.name: Single-study disease-defining report
h_regions.description: The disease is established primarily by one core human study (or a tight preprint-journal pair) that links PSMF1 to a broad phenotypic spectrum; additional AMC8-labeled case reports are not separately indexed in PubMed.

h_regions.name: Variant-level follow-up cluster
h_regions.description: Additional literature, if present, is anchored by the exact pathogenic PSMF1 variant(s) and family-level segregation details from the core report rather than by the AMC8 phenotype label.

h_regions.name: Alternate phenotype alias
h_regions.description: The same PSMF1 disease may be published under a different congenital neuromuscular label, old synonym, or descriptive phenotype that is not AMC8/arthrogryposis in PubMed indexing.

h_regions.name: Split genetics-function literature
h_regions.description: Genetic diagnosis and functional mechanism are distributed across separate papers, with the patient report and the mechanistic study appearing as distinct PubMed records rather than one combined article.

h_regions.name: Paper-anchored orphan label
h_regions.description: The AMC8 label exists in clinical catalogs but PubMed literature is anchored to one gene-discovery paper and a small citation neighborhood, leaving no separately indexed AMC8 case series or cohort.

h_regions.name: Variant-family mining gap
h_regions.description: Any additional literature, if present, is most likely to appear only when searching exact PSMF1 variant nomenclature, pedigree identifiers, or family segregation language rather than phenotype or disease labels.
